<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Eastern Daraa offensive (June 2018)]]
***[[Syrian Army]] troops and [[Liwa al-Quds]] militiamen seize control of the strategic town of [[Busra al-Harir]] in the southern [[Daraa Governorate]]. Around 45,000 people have been displaced in the region due to recent fighting. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-44613943 (BBC)]
**Syrian [[Syrian Arab News Agency|state media]] reports two [[Israel]]i missiles struck targets near [[Damascus International Airport]] overnight, including an [[Iran]]ian cargo plane which had just landed. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/06/syria-israeli-missiles-strike-damascus-airport-180626050523683.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Gaza–Israel conflict]]
**The [[Israeli Air Force]] strikes vehicles it claims were being used to launch incendiary balloons from [[Gaza strip|Gaza]] over the border into [[Israel]]. [https://www.jpost.com/Breaking-News/Israel-Air-Force-strikes-northern-Gaza-560898 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
**[[Israel]]i [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] discusses the conflict with [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] with the [[United Nations]] Special Coordinator to the Middle East Peace Process, [[Nickolay Mladenov]], who has been preparing [[humanitarianism|humanitarian projects]] for Gaza. [https://www.jpost.com/Breaking-News/Netanyahu-talks-Gaza-with-UNs-Mladenov-560893 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
;Business and economy
*[[Economy of Iran]], [[2017–18 Iranian protests]]
**Protests in [[Iran]], particularly the capital, [[Tehran]], enter their second day as thousands of protestors demand action following a collapse in the value of the [[Iranian rial]]. [[President of Iran|President]] [[Hassan Rouhani]] takes to live TV to call the protests "foreign media propaganda" and says the United States is waging "psychological, economic and political war" with Iran. Protestors blame the Iranian government for the crisis, saying billions are being wasted on expensive conflicts. Iran blames sanctions imposed by [[US President]] [[Donald Trump]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/iran-economic-protests-enter-second-day-amid-rials-collapse/ (''The Times of Israel'')] 
**The protests become the biggest in Tehran since [[2011–12 Iranian protests|2012]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/iran-protests-latest-nuclear-deal-donald-trump-sanctions-hassan-rouhani-a8417431.html (''The Independent'')]
;Disasters and accidents
*A van is driven into the headquarters of ''[[De Telegraaf]]'' in [[Amsterdam]], Netherlands. The building is severely damaged in an ensuing fire. Terrorism has not been ruled out. [https://nltimes.nl/2018/06/26/van-crashes-de-telegraaf-building-amsterdam (''NL Times'')]
*Authorities in [[France]] and [[French Polynesia]] meet to discuss rescue plans for MV ''Thorco Lineage'', a freighter hauling [[zinc]] that is grounded with eighteen people on board on a [[coral reef]] near [[Raroia]], [[Tuamotus]]. [https://www.radionz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/360483/authorities-meet-to-plan-rescue-of-ship-stuck-on-french-polynesian-reef (Radio New Zealand)]
*A lorry and a bus collide in [[Guyhirn]], [[Cambridgeshire]], UK. Two people are killed and twelve are injured, five seriously. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-cambridgeshire-44612842 (BBC)]
*[[2018 Tham Luang cave rescue]]
**Navy divers attempting to rescue a children's [[association football|football]] team and their adult coach after they became trapped in Tham Luang Nang Non cave in [[Chiang Rai]], [[Thailand]], on Saturday resume searching after rising waters earlier hampered efforts. They report finding fresh footprints in the cave. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-44610972 (BBC)]
*The [[US]] [[National Transportation Safety Board]] reveals the [[lithium ion]] battery on a [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] [[Tesla Model S|Model S]] involved in a double-fatality crash in [[Florida]] reignited twice after initially being extinguished by firefighters. It also reveals the vehicle was traveling at 116mph when the accident occurred; Tesla has introduced [[speed limiter]]s on their cars as a result. [https://www.engadget.com/2018/06/26/tesla-battery-reignited-twice-after-florida-crash/?guccounter=1 (Engadget)]
*[[Latvia]] opts to describe an ongoing drought as "a natural disaster of a national scale" that can be dealt with using normal laws, in preference over declaring a [[state of emergency]]. [https://eng.lsm.lv/article/politics/politics/latvian-officials-choose-natural-disaster-over-state-of-emergency.a283426/ (LSM)]
;International relations
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**[[Container ship]] MV ''Alexander Maersk'' is allowed by [[Italy|Italian]] authorities to dock in [[Pozzallo]], [[Sicily]], after several days. There, it discharges over 100 rescued migrants. [[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] [[Giuseppe Conte]] says [[Germany|German]] migrant rescue ship MV ''Lifeline'' will be permitted to dock in [[Malta]] in a deal that will see some of the migrants on board come to Italy. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/06/danish-cargo-ship-carrying-refugees-allowed-dock-italy-180626081632471.html (Al Jazeera)]
*An [[Israel]]i official says that the nation has asked [[Cyprus]] to consider allowing Israel to set up a shipping point on the island for goods destined for [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-cyprus-gaza/israel-asks-cyprus-to-consider-shipping-route-for-gaza-cypriot-official-idUSKBN1JM1Z2 (Reuters)]
*The [[Palestinian Authority]] rejects proposals from [[Israel]] and the United States to reduce sanctions that the PA has imposed on [[Hamas]]-controlled [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. The PA says that there is a "conspiracy" afoot to create a "humanitarian issue" out of the disagreements. [https://www.jpost.com/Arab-Israeli-Conflict/Palestinian-Authority-rejects-Israeli-US-ideas-to-help-Gaza-560921 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
;Law and crime
*[[Terrorism in France]]
**[[France|French]] police continue questioning ten suspected far-right terrorists arrested on Saturday over an alleged plot to attack [[Islam|Muslims]]. An extension to their detention was authorised late last night. [https://www.thelocal.fr/20180626/what-we-know-about-the-threat-posed-by-frances-radical-far-right (''The Local'')]
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**[[UK]] citizen Khalid Ali is found guilty at the [[Old Bailey]] in [[London]] of plotting a terror attack after he was found with knives in the city, and of building and detonating bombs for the [[Taliban]] in [[Afghanistan]]. He was detained within metres of [[UK Parliament|Parliament]], and wished to murder [[Members of the UK Parliament|MPs]] and [[Metropolitan Police|police officers]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-44613587 (BBC)] [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/jun/26/taliban-bomb-maker-convicted-of-plotting-to-kill-police-and-mps (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Legal challenges to the Trump travel ban]]
**The [[U.S. Supreme Court]] rules 5–4 in favor of the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]'s [[Presidential Proclamation 9645|September 2017 travel ban]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/06/26/politics/travel-ban-supreme-court/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Trump administration family separation policy]]
**Eighteen attorneys general, representing seventeen U.S. states and [[Washington DC]], sue the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] over migrant family separations at the U.S. border with [[Mexico]]. The litigants demand around 2,000 migrant children be reunited with their families. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-sued-border-children-latest-states-lawsuit-us-mexico-immigration-migrants-separate-families-a8418396.html (''The Independent'')]
;Politics and elections
*[[United States Senate election in Utah, 2018]]
**[[Mitt Romney]] wins the primary elections in [[Utah]], defeating [[Mike Kennedy (politician)|Mike Kennedy]]. [https://www.deseretnews.com/article/900022982/romney-declared-winner-over-kennedy-by-ap-in-senate-race.html (''Deseret News'')]
